summary: Iteration 13 — Full browser-based marquee continuity validation + regression spot checks. Marquee fix (direction:ltr + position:relative on .marquee-section) is CONFIRMED WORKING. Desktop 1440x900: 19/19 samples effectively PASS (one sample reported coverage=1439.99993... vs 1440 — a sub-pixel floating-point rounding artifact, visually full coverage). Mobile 390x844: 19/19 samples PASS. Computed style verified: direction=ltr (not inherited rtl), position=relative, overflow=hidden, .marquee-inner offsetLeft=0 (bug of -2624 is gone). 2 .marquee-content elements present. All 8 regression spot-checks PASS. Zero console errors. One remaining non-blocking Lenis warning (see below).

issues: Union coverage computed as 1439.99993896484 vs viewport 1440 — sub-pixel floating-point rounding on getBoundingClientRect edges. Visually full coverage, two rects abut at x=1352 with widths 2032 each spanning -680→1352→3384. Not a real gap.

Non-blocking (warning, not error) but worth E1 investigating which element Lenis is complaining about.

rca of the issue: Earlier iterations observed empty marquee because the parent <body dir='rtl'> caused the inline-flex .marquee-inner to be laid out starting from the right edge, producing a huge negative offsetLeft (~-2624) that pushed both .marquee-content rows outside the viewport. Fix: forcing .marquee-section { direction: ltr; position: relative; } re-anchors the inner flex layout at x=0 (confirmed: innerOffsetLeft=0 now) and gives Lenis a non-static container. Combined with the dual-row + translate3d(-50%) keyframe this yields seamless coverage.
